newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Late BHP drop hits recovering Australian stocks.
newsitem.headline: Late BHP drop hits recovering Australian stocks.

text.p: The Australian share market turned weaker again in the last half-hour on Friday as bellwether BHP took a new blow when it announced yet another resignation from senior ranks.
BHP and the main share index had all but recovered from early losses but the news reversed the trend and the resource giant's stock ended 45 cents down on the day at A$16.99 (US$12.40).
The All Ordinaries index ended 6.3 points down at 2,711.4 in high total turnover of A$1.066 billion. BHP shares accounted for around 17.5 percent of the value.
BHP has plunged 5.5 percent in two days in reaction to three resignations from the company's senior management.
"This is not looking good. It creates a lot of uncertainty over the future," one senior Sydney-based dealer said.
The third to go was John O'Connor, head of the petroleum division, citing irreconcilable differences between him and the board. The news came just 35 minutes before the market close.
"I'm sure it will take a hit here and overseas tonight, but the underlying assets are good and some people will see it providing ample opportunity to buy," said one BHP analyst.
The number of advancing issues had a slight lead over declines, but few blue chips were found among the gain leaders.
One exception was global miner Rio Tinto, which rose a further 45 cents to A$21.30 as the support for its London sibling held firm and metal prices rose on Thursday.
"Commodities had a reasonable night last night," Richard Herring of Burrell & Co in Birsbane noted.
The banking sector ended 0.24 percent firmer, but stock performance was mixed.

Transport group Brambles was one of the day's weakest stocks, down 70.8 cents at A$28.40. Dealers said investors took home profits after Thursday's four percent rally to a record A$29.40, sparked by good results from its partner in the Chep pallet business, GKN Plc.

Medical instrument designer Polartechnics was Friday's undisputed winner. It surged 75 cents to a record high of A$4.35 in a much delayed reaction to the June announcement of a strategic alliance with Ethicon Inc to commercialise Polartechnics' cancer detection device, the Polarprobe.
